mainTopic: Which acts of עבודה זרה bring the death penalty, the sources for them from the פסוקים, and whether slaughtering or bowing is the model for the whole category.
overview: The משנה lists the acts of עבודה זרה that bring סקילה: worshipping, slaughtering, burning incense, pouring a libation, bowing, accepting an idol as a god, or calling it 'my god.' Acts of honor like hugging, kissing, or dressing an idol, and vowing or swearing in its name, are only a לא תעשה. Degrading acts that are an idol's normal worship, like defecating before בעל פעור or throwing a stone at מרקוליס, count as real worship. רבי ירמיה explains that worship in an idol's usual way makes a person liable, and the four Temple-style acts make a person liable for any idol, even when they are not its usual way. אביי adds that sprinkling blood is included in pouring a libation. A ברייתא finds sources for all four acts. It teaches that slaughtering is the model, so only Temple services bring death, while bowing is a separate case with its own פסוק. The גמרא explains why the ברייתא raised slaughtering קדשים outside the Temple, which brings only כרת. Then רבא בר רב חנן challenges אביי, suggesting that bowing could be the model instead, with זובח teaching that intent can carry over from one service to another. The amud ends as the גמרא begins citing רבי יוחנן on that case, and his ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The acts of idol worship that carry the death penalty
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the acts of עבודה זרה that make a person liable to סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who worships idols is stoned. This includes one who worships, one who slaughters an animal to it, one who burns incense to it, one who pours a libation to it, one who bows to it, one who accepts it as his god, and one who says to it: 'You are my god.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists the actions that count as full idol worship, which are punished with סקילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Four of these acts (slaughtering, burning incense, pouring a libation, bowing) are the kinds of service done for ה׳ in the בית המקדש. The list also includes acts done only with words: accepting the idol as a god, or saying 'You are my god.' The list opens with the general phrase 'one who worships', and the גמרא will soon ask what that phrase adds.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (the opening text the גמרא discusses)
Idol worship
One who slaughters an animal as an offering
One who burns incense or offering parts
One who pours a liquid offering (a libation)
One who bows down

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'stoned' does not appear in this line. The משנה is continuing an earlier list of people who are punished with סקילה, so that punishment is understood.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who worships idols [is stoned]:
phrases.notes: This carries on the earlier משנה that listed the people punished with סקילה, so 'is stoned' is understood here.

phrases.english: both one who worships, and one who slaughters [an offering],
and one who burns incense, and one who pours a libation,
and one who bows down,
and one who accepts it upon himself as a god,
and one who says to it: 'You are my god.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הָעוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֶחָד הָעוֹבֵד וְאֶחָד הַמְזַבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of the משנה on עבודה זרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Worshipping, slaughtering, burning incense, pouring a libation, bowing, accepting an idol as a god, or saying 'You are my god' makes one liable to סקילה.

steps.title: Acts of honor and vows that are only a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: Acts of honoring an idol, and vowing or swearing in its name, are forbidden but do not carry the death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: But one who hugs it, kisses it, cleans it, sprays water before it, washes it, anoints it with oil, dresses it, or puts shoes on it transgresses a לא תעשה. One who vows in its name or swears in its name also transgresses a לא תעשה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now lists actions that show honor or respect to an idol. They are forbidden, but they are not punished by death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אבל ('but') signals a contrast with the list in step 1. Hugging, kissing, and the other acts are ways of honoring the idol, not the kinds of worship listed above, so they are only a לא תעשה. Vowing or swearing by the idol's name is also forbidden, but it too is only a לא תעשה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who hugs
One who sprays water on the floor (to settle the dust)
One who puts shoes on (the idol)
Transgresses a negative commandment (no death penalty)
One who confirms his words with an oath in its name

steps.confusionAlert: These acts are still completely forbidden. The only difference is that they do not bring the death penalty.

phrases.english: But one who hugs [it], or one who kisses [it],
or one who sweeps [before it], or one who sprays water [before it],
or one who washes [it], or one who anoints [it with oil],
or one who dresses [it], or one who puts shoes on [it]
transgresses a prohibition.
One who vows in its name, or one who confirms [his words with an oath] in its name
transgresses a prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 1 by listing forbidden acts that do not carry the death penalty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Honoring an idol (hugging, kissing, cleaning, washing, anointing, dressing, putting shoes on it) and vowing or swearing in its name are only a לא תעשה.

steps.title: Degrading acts that are the idol's normal worship
steps.stepSummary: If an idol's normal worship is a degrading act, doing that act is real worship: defecating before בעל פעור, or throwing a stone at מרקוליס.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who defecates before בעל פעור: that is its worship. One who throws a stone at מרקוליס: that is its worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה teaches that even a disgusting or insulting act counts as worship when that act is how this idol is normally served.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think defecating or throwing a stone is an insult to the idol, not worship. The משנה says that because this is the way these idols are normally served, doing it is real worship. The key is how the idol is normally served, not how the act looks to us.

keyTerms.meaning: One who uncovers himself to defecate
An idol worshipped by defecating before it
Mercury, an idol worshipped by throwing stones at it
That is its (normal) form of worship

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has three levels: (1) the listed acts of worship bring סקילה; (2) acts of honor and vows in an idol's name are only a לא תעשה; (3) an idol's normal way of being served counts as worship, even if the act is degrading.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key principle for the whole topic: the idol's normal way of being served counts as worship, even when the act seems disrespectful.

phrases.english: One who uncovers himself [and defecates] before בעל פעור
this is its worship.
One who throws a stone at Mercury
this is its worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַפּוֹעֵר עַצְמוֹ לְבַעַל פְּעוֹר זוֹ הִיא עֲבוֹדָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds that an idol's normal way of being served counts as worship, even if the act is degrading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Defecating before בעל פעור or throwing a stone at מרקוליס is worship, because that is how each of these idols is normally served.

steps.title: What does 'one who worships' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the phrase אחד העובד adds to the משנה's list.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'one who worships'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question about the wording of the משנה. This sets up an explanation that comes in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Worship' sounds like a general word that covers everything in the list. So why list 'one who worships' as its own item next to slaughtering, burning incense, and the rest? The גמרא wants to know which specific case this phrase includes.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה
What? (asking what something means or includes)
'Both one who worships' (the opening item in the משנה's list)

phrases.english: Gemara:
What is [meant by] 'one who worships'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the opening phrase of the משנה (step 1) and questions why it is needed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case of worship the phrase 'אחד העובד' includes, beyond the specific acts that follow it in the list.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: worshipping in its usual way, plus four acts even when unusual
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה reads the משנה as two parts. Worshipping an idol in its usual way makes a person liable. The four acts of זביחה, קיטור, ניסוך and השתחואה make a person liable even when they are not that idol's usual way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: This is what the משנה means. One who worships an idol the way it is normally worshipped is liable. Also, one who slaughters, burns incense, pours a libation, or bows down is liable, even if that is not the idol's normal way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question from Step 4 about what אחד העובד means. רבי ירמיה says it means worship done in the idol's own usual way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate rules here. Any act that is this idol's normal worship makes a person liable. The four listed acts make a person liable for any idol at all, even one that is never worshipped that way.

keyTerms.meaning: In its usual way: the normal manner this idol is worshipped
Not in its usual way
One who slaughters an offering
One who burns incense or an offering
One who pours a libation
One who bows down

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the list as only usual-way worship. The four acts make a person liable even when they are NOT the idol's usual way. That is the whole point of וַאֲפִילּוּ שֶׁלֹּא כְּדַרְכָּהּ.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the two-part rule that the rest of the סוגיא will look for a source for: usual-way worship, plus the four acts that count for every idol.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said: This is what it is saying,
One who worships it in its usual way,
and one who slaughters, and one who burns incense,
and one who pours a libation, and one who bows down,
and even if it is not its usual way.
phrases.notes: This last phrase goes on the four acts just listed, not on the first one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 4 by reading the משנה as two parts.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אחד העובד means usual-way worship. The four listed acts make a person liable even when they are not the usual way.

steps.title: Why isn't sprinkling blood on the list?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה does not also list זריקה, sprinkling the blood, as one of the acts that count even when unusual.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let the משנה also count one who sprinkles blood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the list in the משנה. It asks why sprinkling blood was left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the four acts count because they are like the service in the בית המקדש, then sprinkling blood is also part of that service. So it seems it should be on the list too.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sprinkles or throws the blood of an offering
Let it count or list

phrases.english: And let it also count one who sprinkles?
phrases.notes: He means sprinkling the blood of the offering, which is another step of the בית המקדש service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the list as רבי ירמיה explained it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the משנה's list of four acts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sprinkling blood is also part of the service, so leaving it off makes the list seem incomplete.

steps.title: אביי: sprinkling counts as pouring
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that זריקה is included in ניסוך, because a פסוק calls blood a libation.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Sprinkling is the same as pouring a libation, as it is written: 'I will not pour their libations of blood.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. Sprinkling is not listed separately because it is already included in pouring a libation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the word for pouring a libation about blood. That shows sprinkling blood is a kind of ניסוך, so the list does not need to name it again.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as
Their libations

phrases.english: Abaye said: Sprinkling is the same as pouring a libation,
as it is written: 'I will not pour their libations of blood.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 16:4

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Inclusion: the missing item is already part of an item on the list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sprinkling seemed to be a separate act that was left off the list.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sprinkling is a form of ניסוך, so it is already covered.

steps.title: What is the source for this rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that these acts make a person liable even when they are not the idol's usual way.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these matters learned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for the source of the rule. This line sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we have the rule, but not where it comes from. The גמרא wants a פסוק showing that these acts count as idol worship even for an idol that is not usually worshipped that way.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters learned?

phrases.english: From where are these matters learned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the list to asking where the rule comes from.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A Torah source showing that the four acts make a person liable even when they are not the idol's usual way.

steps.title: The ברייתא: the פסוק is about slaughtering to an idol
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the words לאלהים in the פסוק show it is about slaughtering to an idol. Without those words, the פסוק could be read as being about slaughtering a קרבן outside the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the חכמים taught: If it only said 'One who slaughters shall be destroyed,' I would have said the פסוק is talking about one who slaughters a קרבן outside. So the פסוק says 'to the gods,' to show it is talking about one who slaughters to an idol.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by quoting a ברייתא. The first part only shows that the פסוק is about idol worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the word לאלהים, the punishment could have meant the sin of slaughtering a קרבן outside the בית המקדש. The word לאלהים points the פסוק toward idol worship instead. This is the first step of the source, and the ברייתא continues past this point.

keyTerms.meaning: One who slaughters shall be destroyed
Slaughtering a קרבן outside the בית המקדש courtyard
Therefore the פסוק says
To the gods, meaning to idols

steps.confusionAlert: This part of the ברייתא does not yet prove the 'even when not its usual way' rule. It only shows the פסוק is about idols. Steps 10-19 finish the proof.

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
If it had said only: 'One who slaughters shall be destroyed,'
phrases.notes: שמות 22:19. The full פסוק says one who slaughters to the gods shall be destroyed.

phrases.english: I would have said it is about one who slaughters sacrificial animals outside;
phrases.notes: Outside means outside the בית המקדש courtyard.

phrases.english: that is what the פסוק is talking about.
Therefore the פסוק says: 'to the gods,'
the פסוק is talking about one who slaughters to an idol.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to Step 8 by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source begins with the פסוק זובח לאלהים. The word לאלהים shows the פסוק is about slaughtering to an idol, not slaughtering a קרבן outside.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that these acts make a person liable in idol worship
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 22:19, as explained in a ברייתא

steps.title: What about burning and pouring?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the פסוק only mentions slaughtering. It asks where we learn that קיטור and ניסוך also make a person liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: So far I only know about someone who slaughters to an idol. Where do we learn the same about someone who burns incense or pours a libation?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא points out a gap: its פסוק only talks about slaughtering. It asks for a source for the other acts, setting up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 showed that זובח לאלהים is about an idol. But the word זובח only covers זביחה. The ברייתא now looks for a source for קיטור and ניסוך, two of the four acts in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: I only know (from this source) about…
one who burns incense or offerings (קיטור)
one who pours a libation (ניסוך)
from where do we know?

phrases.english: I only know about one who slaughters;
phrases.notes: From the פסוק in the last step, which only says זובח, someone who slaughters.

phrases.english: one who burns or pours, from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בְּזוֹבֵחַ, מְקַטֵּר וּמְנַסֵּךְ מִנַּיִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that the source in step 9 only covers slaughtering.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that קיטור and ניסוך to an idol also bring the death penalty.

steps.title: Every Temple service belongs to ה׳ alone
steps.stepSummary: The words בלתי לה' לבדו teach that all the Temple services are reserved for ה' alone. So doing any of them for an idol makes a person liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "Except to ה' alone." It set aside all the services for the special Name of ה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers from the end of the same פסוק: "except to ה' alone."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לבדו, "alone," tells us that every Temple service is only for ה', not just slaughtering. So doing any of these services, like burning or pouring, for an idol falls under the same punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: except to ה' alone
emptied out, set aside
the services done in the בית המקדש
the special Name of ה'

phrases.english: The verse says: "Except to the Lord alone."
phrases.notes: The end of the same פסוק, שמות 22:19.

phrases.english: It set aside all the services
phrases.notes: Literally "emptied out." He means the פסוק reserved every service only for ה'.

phrases.english: for the special Name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: לה' לבדו reserves all Temple services for ה', so קיטור and ניסוך to an idol are punished like זביחה.

steps.title: How is bowing included?
steps.stepSummary: Slaughtering was used to stand for all the Temple services. Bowing is not a Temple service, so the ברייתא asks where we learn that bowing is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since slaughtering was singled out to teach about the services done inside the בית המקדש, where do we learn to include bowing?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a new question about השתחואה, the fourth act in the משנה, and sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lesson from the last step only covers Temple services, like slaughtering, burning and pouring. Bowing is not one of those services, so that lesson cannot cover it. A separate source is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: since it was singled out
services done inside the בית המקדש
to include
bowing down

steps.confusionAlert: Bowing is not left out because it is less serious. It is left out of the first lesson only because that lesson is about Temple services, and bowing is not one of them.

phrases.english: Since slaughtering was singled out
to teach about the services done inside,
phrases.notes: Slaughtering stands as the example for all the services done in the בית המקדש, and bowing isn't one of them.

phrases.english: from where do we include bowing?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁיָּצְאָה זְבִיחָה לִידּוֹן בַּעֲבוֹדוֹת פְּנִים, מִנַּיִין לְרַבּוֹת הִשְׁתַּחֲוָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the lesson of step 11 does not reach bowing.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that bowing to an idol brings the death penalty, even though it is not a Temple service.

steps.title: Bowing learned from two פסוקים side by side
steps.stepSummary: One פסוק mentions bowing to other gods, and the פסוק right near it says to take that person out to be stoned. Putting them together teaches the death penalty for bowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "And he went and served other gods and bowed to them." Right near it, it says: "Then you shall bring out that man…" to be stoned.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers by joining two nearby פסוקים: one about bowing, and one about stoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק names bowing as a way of serving idols. The פסוק next to it gives the punishment of stoning. Because they sit next to each other, the punishment applies to bowing.

keyTerms.meaning: and bowed to them
right next to it
and you shall bring out (to be punished)

phrases.english: The verse says: "And he went and served other gods
phrases.notes: דברים 17:3

phrases.english: and bowed to them,"
and next to it is written:
"Then you shall bring out that man, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 17:5. The rest of the פסוק says to stone that person.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וַיֵּלֶךְ וַיַּעֲבֹד אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים וַיִּשְׁתַּחוּ לָהֶם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Bowing is named next to the stoning punishment in דברים 17, so bowing brings the death penalty.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why השתחואה counts as one of the four acts in the משנה, even though it is not a Temple service.

steps.title: We have the punishment, but where is the warning?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא now has the punishment for bowing. It asks where the Torah actually forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have heard the punishment. Where is the warning?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks for a separate prohibition against bowing, setting up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah normally gives both an עונש, a punishment, and an אזהרה, a warning that forbids the act. The last step gave only the punishment. Now the ברייתא looks for the warning.

keyTerms.meaning: the punishment
the warning, the actual prohibition
we have heard, we have learned

steps.confusionAlert: Knowing the punishment is not enough. The Torah also needs to say "do not do this" before someone can be punished.

phrases.english: We have heard the punishment;
the warning, from where?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the punishment found in step 13 and asks for the matching prohibition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that forbids bowing to an idol.

steps.title: The warning: do not bow to another god
steps.stepSummary: The warning comes from the פסוק "For you shall not bow to another god."
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "For you shall not bow to another god."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the פסוק that forbids bowing to an idol and finishes its search for sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק directly says not to bow to another god. Together with step 13, bowing now has both a punishment and a warning.

keyTerms.meaning: you shall not bow
to another god

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא finds sources for all four acts in the משנה. זביחה comes from זובח לאלהים. קיטור and ניסוך come from לה' לבדו. השתחואה gets its punishment from the nearby פסוקים in דברים 17, and its warning from "לא תשתחוה לאל אחר."

phrases.english: The verse says:
"For you shall not bow to another god."
phrases.notes: שמות 34:14

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״כִּי לֹא תִשְׁתַּחֲוֶה לְאֵל אַחֵר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The warning against bowing comes from "כי לא תשתחוה לאל אחר" (שמות 34:14).

steps.title: Maybe hugging, kissing, and dressing an idol are included too
steps.stepSummary: Bowing was included even though it is not a Temple service. So the ברייתא asks whether other honors, like hugging, kissing, or putting shoes on an idol, should also bring the death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think I should also include someone who hugs an idol, kisses it, or puts shoes on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible worry. Since bowing was added, maybe every kind of honor to an idol is punished by death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 12-15 showed that bowing gets the death penalty even though it is not a Temple service. That opens a door: if a non-Temple act counts, maybe all acts of honor count. The ברייתא is testing how far that goes.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought (opens a possibility that will be rejected)
Include
One who hugs (an idol)
One who kisses (an idol)
One who puts shoes on (an idol)

phrases.english: One might think that I should include
one who hugs, one who kisses, and one who puts shoes on an idol?
phrases.notes: He means: should these people also get the death penalty, just like someone who bows?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the inclusion of bowing and asks whether other non-Temple honors are included too.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether non-Temple honors such as hugging, kissing, or dressing an idol also bring the death penalty.

steps.title: The word "slaughters" rules them out
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the פסוק's word "זובח" (one who slaughters). This word limits the death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the פסוק says: "One who slaughters."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question by pointing to one word in the פסוק. The next step explains how that word does the job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק "זובח לאלהים יחרם" names slaughtering on purpose. That one word is the key that will limit the death penalty to Temple-style acts. Hugging and kissing are not like that, so they are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore the פסוק says (introduces the source that answers)
One who slaughters (an offering)

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says: "One who slaughters."
phrases.notes: שמות 22:19

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16 by citing the word זובח.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word זובח limits the death penalty, so hugging, kissing, and dressing an idol are not included.

steps.title: Why slaughtering was singled out: only Temple services bring death
steps.stepSummary: Slaughtering was already part of the general group of forbidden idol worship. It was mentioned separately to serve as a model: only acts that are Temple services (עבודת פנים) bring the death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Slaughtering was already included in the general group. So why was it named separately? To compare others to it and tell you: slaughtering is special because it is a service done inside the Temple, and you get death for it. So too, anything that is a service done inside the Temple gets death.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains how the word "זובח" works. Slaughtering is a sample case that shows what kind of act gets the death penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering was already part of the general group of forbidden worship, so naming it separately must teach something new. It sets the rule: death applies only to acts that are Temple services. Hugging and kissing are not, so they are out.

keyTerms.meaning: It was included in the general group
So why was it singled out?
To compare (other cases) to it
A service done inside the Temple
Just as ... so too (building a rule from one example)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying slaughtering is the only forbidden act. Slaughtering is a sample that defines the group: any Temple-style service brings death.

phrases.english: Slaughtering was already in the general group,
so why was it singled out?
To compare others to it and tell you:
Just as slaughtering is special
in that it is a service done inside the Temple
and one gets the death penalty for it,
so too, anything that is a service done inside the Temple
one gets the death penalty for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the word זובח from step 17 limits the death penalty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only acts that are Temple services (עבודת פנים) done for an idol bring the death penalty.

steps.title: Bowing is its own case; slaughtering sets the rule for the rest
steps.stepSummary: Bowing was singled out to give it its own death penalty, even though it is not a Temple service. Slaughtering was singled out to set the rule for everything else.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bowing was singled out to be judged on its own. Slaughtering was singled out to teach about the whole group.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא wraps up the section. It explains how bowing and slaughtering each play a different role.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could ask: if only Temple services bring death, why does bowing? The answer is that bowing has its own פסוק (steps 13 and 15), so it is a stand-alone exception. It does not open the door to hugging or kissing. Slaughtering is the model for everything else.

keyTerms.meaning: Was singled out to be judged on its own
Bowing
To teach about the whole group

steps.whatToRemember: For an idol, death comes for (1) any Temple-style service, modeled on slaughtering, and (2) bowing, which has its own פסוק. Hugging, kissing, and dressing an idol are forbidden but do not bring death.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic rule for which acts of עבודה זרה are capital crimes.

phrases.english: Bowing was singled out to be judged on its own,

phrases.aramaic: יָצְאָה זְבִיחָה לִידּוֹן עַל הַכְּלָל כּוּלּוֹ.
phrases.english: and slaughtering was singled out to teach about the whole group.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles how bowing fits with the Temple-service rule of step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Bowing is a stand-alone exception with its own source. Slaughtering defines the general rule that only Temple services bring death.

steps.title: Slaughtering קדשים outside the Temple is כרת, not death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now examines the ברייתא. It quotes the ברייתא's earlier idea that the פסוק might be about slaughtering קדשים outside the Temple. It objects that this sin is punished with כרת, not death.
steps.simpleTranslation: The master said: "I would have said the פסוק is talking about someone who slaughters holy offerings outside the Temple." But that sin is punished with כרת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops quoting the ברייתא and begins to question it. It challenges one line from earlier in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק "זובח לאלהים יחרם" speaks of a death penalty. Earlier, the ברייתא suggested it might mean slaughtering קדשים outside the Temple. But the Torah already gives that sin a different punishment, כרת. So how could anyone have thought this פסוק was about it?

keyTerms.meaning: Holy offerings
Outside (the Temple courtyard)
Being cut off, a punishment from Heaven, not a court death penalty

steps.confusionAlert: כרת and the court's death penalty are different punishments. The question only works because the פסוק talks about death, while slaughtering outside is punished with כרת.

phrases.english: The master said: I would have said
phrases.notes: "The master" is the teacher of the ברייתא; the גמרא is quoting a line from earlier in it.

phrases.english: that the verse speaks of one who slaughters holy offerings outside the Temple.
But one who slaughters holy offerings outside gets כרת!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:8-9

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: הָיִיתִי אוֹמֵר בְּזוֹבֵחַ קֳדָשִׁים בַּחוּץ הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the ברייתא, the גמרא goes back to examine one of its earlier lines.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's earlier idea that the פסוק "זובח לאלהים יחרם" might be about slaughtering קדשים outside the Temple.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That sin already has a set punishment, כרת. A פסוק that gives a death penalty could not have been about it.

steps.title: The ברייתא needed to rule out the death penalty even with a warning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers step 20: someone might have thought that slaughtering קדשים outside the Temple brings death if the sinner was warned, and כרת only without a warning. The ברייתא teaches that it is only כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: if witnesses warned him, he gets the death penalty, and if they did not warn him, he gets כרת. So the ברייתא teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא bothered to mention slaughtering קדשים outside the Temple at all, since everyone knows it carries כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In many sins, a warning (התראה) is what turns a כרת sin into a court death penalty. So one might think a warned person who slaughters outside the Temple gets death. The ברייתא's point is that even with a warning, this sin stays at כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: It would have entered your mind to say (a mistaken first thought)
They warned him (witnesses gave a warning before the sin)
Death penalty by a court
Being cut off, a punishment from Heaven
It teaches us (the ruling comes to reject the mistaken idea)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא was not unsure whether this sin is כרת. Its question was whether a warning might raise it to a court death penalty, and the answer is no.

phrases.english: It would have entered your mind to say:
When they warned him — death;
phrases.notes: This means witnesses warned him before he slaughtered the קדשים outside the Temple.

phrases.english: When they did not warn him — כרת.
So it teaches us (that this is not so).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains a needed teaching by showing a mistaken first thought it rules out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A warned person who slaughters קדשים outside the Temple gets the death penalty; an unwarned one gets כרת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with a warning, slaughtering קדשים outside the Temple brings only כרת, never death.

steps.title: Maybe bowing is the model for all forms of worship
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב חנן asks אביי: why not say that bowing was singled out to teach about the whole category, so that any respectful act of worship to an idol brings death?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב חנן said to אביי: Say instead that bowing was singled out to teach about the entire category.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר רב חנן challenges how the ברייתא read the פסוק. He suggests flipping the model: bowing, not slaughtering, sets the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said slaughtering is the model, so only Temple-type services bring death. Bowing is not a Temple service, so if bowing were the model, every honorable act of worship (like hugging or kissing) would bring death. That would erase the limit the ברייתא set in steps 17-18.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead (proposing a different reading)
Bowing down
Was singled out to teach about the entire general category

steps.whyThisMatters: If this challenge succeeds, the line between Temple-style services and other acts of honor would disappear.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר רַב חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Ḥanan said to Abaye:
Say that bowing was singled out
to teach about the entire category.
phrases.notes: He means: any act of honor done for an idol would bring death, just like bowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר רַב חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי: אֵימָא, יָצְאָה הִשְׁתַּחֲוָאָה לְלַמֵּד עַל הַכְּלָל כּוּלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against the ברייתא's derivation from זובח
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule (steps 18-19) that זובח is the model and bowing is only an exception
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bowing could just as well be the model; since bowing is not a Temple service, all acts of honor would carry death.

steps.title: Then זובח teaches its own lesson about intent
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב חנן blocks the obvious reply. If you ask why the פסוק mentions זובח, the answer is that it teaches something about slaughtering itself: intent for one service carries over to another.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you ask: why do I need זובח? It is needed for itself, to teach that one can have intent from one service to another service.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר רב חנן is still building his challenge. He answers ahead of time the question of why זובח would be needed if bowing were the model.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's answer to him would be: if bowing is the model, the word זובח is extra. He replies that זובח has its own job. It teaches that slaughtering with idol-worship intent for a different service, like sprinkling the blood, still brings death.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (bringing up a possible reply)
Why do I need it?
For itself (to teach something about its own case)
Intent carries over from one service to another

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא answering רבא בר רב חנן. He is still speaking and filling a hole in his own challenge.

phrases.english: And if you will say: why do I need "one who slaughters"?
It is for itself: that one can have intent from one service to another service.
phrases.notes: He means he slaughters now while planning to use the blood or fat for an idol later.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: זוֹבֵחַ לְמָה לִי? לְגוּפֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and protects the challenge of step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the word זובח a different job so it is not extra
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If bowing is the model, the word זובח would serve no purpose.
steps.terutzMaskana: זובח teaches that slaughtering with intent for a later idol service brings death.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא could reply that if bowing were the model, the word זובח would be extra. But זובח is needed for its own lesson, that intent carries over from one service to another. So bowing can still be the model for all honorable worship.
steps.kashyaTarget: The expected defense of the ברייתא: that if bowing were the model, the word זובח in the פסוק would serve no purpose.

steps.title: Bringing a source: רבי יוחנן on slaughtering with intent for another service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a known case to show the idea of intent carrying over: someone slaughters an animal planning to sprinkle its blood or burn its fat for an idol. רבי יוחנן's ruling begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: one who slaughters an animal in order to sprinkle its blood for idol worship or to burn its fat for idol worship, רבי יוחנן says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a source for the idea of intent from one service to another. The case is laid out here, and רבי יוחנן's ruling continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the slaughtering is done with an idol-worship plan that is about later services, not the slaughter itself. This is exactly the case the word זובח was said to teach. רבי יוחנן's ruling will show how this intent is treated.

keyTerms.meaning: To sprinkle its blood (a Temple service)
To burn its fats (a Temple service)

phrases.english: As it was stated: one who slaughters an animal
in order to sprinkle its blood for idol worship
or to burn its fat for idol worship,
Rabbi Yoḥanan says:

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִיתְּמַר: הַשּׁוֹחֵט בְּהֵמָה לִזְרוֹק דָּמָהּ לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for the idea of intent from one service to another raised in step 23
steps.raayaObject: The idea that intent for one service carries over to another
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ruling of the אמוראים, given by רבי יוחנן, about slaughtering with intent to sprinkle blood or burn fat for idol worship
